# Wibeset

> Wibeset is a small studio in Saguenay, Québec, Canada, that builds web and mobile products — the calm, fast, private kind — and ships them itself.

Wibeset was founded by Dominic Martineau (https://dominicmartineau.com), a full
stack developer based in Saguenay, Québec. The studio works in English and
French, and releases the products below under its own name.

## Key facts
- Location: Saguenay, Québec, Canada.
- Founder: Dominic Martineau.
- Working languages: English and French. The site exists in both (/ and /fr/).
- Contact: hello@wibeset.ca
- Focus: web and mobile applications, plus native macOS apps.
- Three of the five products below are not released yet; two are available now.

## Products

- **Puuunch** — A fast, beautiful timesheet for freelancers and small teams. Log
  time, review the week, and send it for approval, without the accounting-software
  feel. Web application. **Not released yet.**
- **Noue** — A collaborative memory for small teams, built on one principle: one
  interaction, one note. A person is a name and a timeline. Made for small
  businesses, agencies and consultants who find HubSpot and Salesforce far too
  complex. Explicitly **not** a CRM. Web application. **Not released yet.**
- **The Chirp League** — Fantasy hockey pools with built-in trash talk: draft real
  NHL players, track live standings against live NHL data, and chirp your rivals
  in one place. Web application, with iOS and Android builds. **Not released yet.**
- **Luere** (https://luere.app, French: https://luere.app/fr/) — A free, native
  macOS app that shrinks, converts, crops and resizes images, with a live
  before/after compare slider. Supports JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC, TIFF and
  GIF. Requires macOS 26 or later. Everything runs on the user's Mac — nothing
  is ever uploaded. Available now.
- **Luere Icon Studio** (https://luere.app/icon-studio/, French:
  https://luere.app/fr/icon-studio/) — A free, native macOS app that turns a
  single logo into every icon and favicon size for web, macOS, iOS and Windows,
  including `favicon.ico`, PWA maskable icons, `.icns` and Xcode
  `AppIcon.appiconset` bundles. Requires macOS 14 or later. Runs entirely on the
  user's Mac. Available now.
